candidates.violated_requirement: Gray-to-binary conversion should use XOR operations between adjacent bits. Replacing XOR with AND will cause incorrect binary conversion when both input bits are 1, leading to wrong Gray code output after the full conversion cycle.
candidates.spec_basis: The implementation should follow the process of converting Gray code to binary representation using XOR operations between adjacent bits

candidates.violated_requirement: Gray-to-binary conversion requires XOR operations between adjacent bits. Using OR instead will produce incorrect binary values when either input bit is 1, causing wrong Gray code output after the full conversion cycle.
candidates.spec_basis: The implementation should follow the process of converting Gray code to binary representation using XOR operations between adjacent bits

candidates.violated_requirement: Gray-to-binary conversion requires each bit to be XORed with the previously converted bit. Using gray_wire[1] instead of bin_out[1] breaks the sequential conversion chain, leading to incorrect binary values and wrong Gray code output.
candidates.spec_basis: The implementation should follow the process of converting Gray code to binary representation using XOR operations between adjacent bits

candidates.violated_requirement: Binary-to-Gray conversion requires XOR operation between the binary value and its right-shifted version. Using OR instead will produce incorrect Gray code when both corresponding bits are 1, violating the single-bit change property between consecutive values.
candidates.spec_basis: The implementation should convert the incremented binary back to Gray code using XOR operation
